# Lab 3.1: Load a Local File

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a CSV file, upload it through the console with schema auto-detect, then load a file with bad rows from the CLI using `max_bad_records`.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Create the dataset and two CSV files.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq --location=US mk --dataset $PROJECT_ID:lab03
cat &gt; stores.csv &lt;&lt;'EOF'
store_id,city,opened_on,monthly_sales
1,Surat,2021-04-01,125000.50
2,Mumbai,2020-11-15,310000.00
3,Pune,2022-01-10,98000.75
EOF
cat &gt; stores_bad.csv &lt;&lt;'EOF'
store_id,city,opened_on,monthly_sales
4,Delhi,2023-02-01,150000
5,Chennai,not-a-date,99000
6,Kolkata,2023-05-12,abc
7,Jaipur,2024-01-20,87000
EOF</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Click **⋮ → Download** in Cloud Shell to save `stores.csv` to your computer.

2. **[Console] Upload with auto-detect.** On `lab03` click **⋮ → Create table**:
   - **Create table from**: Upload → choose `stores.csv`
   - **File format**: CSV
   - **Table**: `stores`
   - **Schema**: tick **Auto detect**
   - **Advanced options → Header rows to skip**: `1`

   Click **Create table** and check the detected schema (`DATE` and `FLOAT` were found automatically).

3. **[CLI] Load the bad file and watch it fail.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq load --source_format=CSV --skip_leading_rows=1 --autodetect lab03.stores_bad stores_bad.csv</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[CLI] Load again, allowing up to 2 bad rows, with an explicit schema.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq load --source_format=CSV --skip_leading_rows=1 --max_bad_records=2 \
  lab03.stores_bad stores_bad.csv \
  store_id:INT64,city:STRING,opened_on:DATE,monthly_sales:NUMERIC
bq head lab03.stores_bad</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[Console] Read the job errors.** Open the load job in **Personal history**. The job succeeded with warnings, and lists the two skipped rows.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| `stores` | 3 rows, schema auto-detected |
| First bad load | Fails on the first bad row |
| Second bad load | 2 rows loaded, 2 skipped |
| Load jobs | Free (shared slot pool) |
